questions.stem: According to the kinetic particle model, all matter is made of:

options.text: Stationary atoms arranged in fixed positions

questions.explanation: The kinetic particle model states that all matter is made of tiny particles (atoms or molecules) that are constantly moving and have kinetic energy.

questions.stem: What happens to the kinetic energy of particles when the temperature increases?
questions.explanation: Higher temperature means particles move faster, so they have more kinetic energy. Temperature is directly related to the average kinetic energy of particles.

options.text: Are far apart with no forces between them

questions.explanation: In a solid, particles are closely packed in a regular pattern and vibrate about fixed positions. They are held together by strong forces of attraction.

questions.stem: In which state of matter are particles furthest apart?

options.text: Particles are equally spaced in all states

questions.explanation: In a gas, particles are far apart (mostly empty space), move randomly at high speeds, and have very weak forces of attraction between them.

questions.stem: Which statement correctly describes particles in a liquid?

options.text: They are far apart and move randomly
They are close together but can move around each other

questions.explanation: In a liquid, particles are close together but not in a regular pattern. They can move around each other, which is why liquids can flow.

questions.stem: The kinetic particle model explains that gas pressure is caused by:

options.text: Gas particles being packed closely together
Gas particles colliding with the walls of their container

questions.explanation: Gas pressure is caused by billions of gas particles colliding with the walls of their container every second, each exerting a tiny force.

questions.stem: Which state of matter has a fixed shape and a fixed volume?

options.text: All states have fixed shape and volume

questions.explanation: Solids have a fixed shape and fixed volume because their particles are held in place by strong forces and vibrate in fixed positions.
